content: 1. Kranzler K, Afnan-Holmes H, Tomlin K, et al. conducted a systematic review to evaluate the benefits of screening for active tuberculosis disease, focusing on its impact on both communities and individuals. This study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013, volume 17, issue 7, pages 856-865. 2. Lönnroth K, Corbett E, Golub J, et al. explored the rationale, definitions, and key considerations for systematic screening of active tuberculosis. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013, volume 17, issue 4, pages 432-446. 3. Uplekar M, Creswell J, Ottmani SE, Weil D, Sahu S, Lönnroth K. discussed programmatic approaches to screening for active tuberculosis in their publication in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013, volume 17, issue 10, pages 1248-1256. 4. Zennner D, Southern J, van Hest R, et al. examined active case finding for tuberculosis among high-risk groups in low-incidence countries. Their research was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013, volume 17, issue 5, pages 573-582. 5. The World Health Organization (WHO) released recommendations in 2012 for investigating contacts of individuals with infectious tuberculosis in lowand middle-income countries, providing guidance for effective contact tracing. 6. In 2011, the WHO published an overview of approaches, guidelines, and tools for the early detection of tuberculosis, emphasizing the importance of timely diagnosis and intervention. 7. The WHO issued guidance in 2006 on engaging all healthcare providers in tuberculosis control, focusing on implementing public-private mix approaches to enhance TB care and management. 8. The WHO introduced the Practical Approach to Lung Health (PAL) in 2005, a primary healthcare strategy aimed at the integrated management of respiratory conditions in individuals aged five years and older. 9. In 2007, the WHO provided recommendations for improving the diagnosis and treatment of smear-negative pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis among adults and adolescents, particularly in HIV-prevalent and resource-constrained settings. 10. The WHO published a guide in 2011 for the rapid implementation of the Xpert MTB/RIF diagnostic test, offering technical and operational considerations for its effective use. 11. The WHO released a handbook in 2011 on conducting tuberculosis prevalence surveys, providing detailed methodologies for assessing the burden of TB in various populations. 12. In 2014, the WHO published a guide on understanding and using tuberculosis data, aimed at improving data-driven decision-making in TB control programs. 13. The WHO developed a framework in 2014 for conducting reviews of tuberculosis programs, offering structured guidance for evaluating and improving program performance. 14. The WHO introduced a tool in 2007 for national situation assessment of public-private mix approaches for TB care and control, facilitating collaboration between public and private sectors. 15. In 2012, the WHO launched the ENGAGE-TB initiative, which integrates community-based tuberculosis activities into the work of nongovernmental and civil society organizations. 16. The Tuberculosis Coalition for Technical Assistance developed a tool in 2008 to estimate the costs incurred by TB patients, helping to address financial barriers to care. 17. The WHO published guiding principles in 2008 for national tuberculosis programs to contribute to health system strengthening, emphasizing the integration of TB services into broader health systems. 18. In 2015, the WHO released guidelines on the management of latent tuberculosis infection, providing evidence-based recommendations for identifying and treating individuals at risk of developing active TB. 19. The WHO updated its guidelines in 2011 for the programmatic management of drug-resistant tuberculosis, addressing the challenges of multidrug-resistant TB. 20. In 2010, the WHO issued guidelines for intensified tuberculosis case-finding and isoniazid preventive therapy for people living with HIV in resource-constrained settings, aiming to reduce TB-related morbidity and mortality. 21. Blok L, Creswell J, Stevens R, et al. proposed a pragmatic approach to measuring, monitoring, and evaluating interventions for improved tuberculosis case detection. Their study was published in International Health in 2014, volume 6, issue 3, pages 181-188. 22. Nishikiori N, Van Weezebeek C. developed a tool to support country-level project planning for active case-finding of pulmonary tuberculosis, focusing on target prioritization and strategy selection. This was published in BMC Public Health in 2013. 23. Van ’t Hoog AH, Onozaki I, Lönnroth K. conducted a modeling study to compare the yield, predictive value, and diagnostic burden of different algorithms for TB screening. Their findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2014, volume 14, article 532. 24. Annex 1 of the WHO guidelines outlines ten potential screening and diagnostic algorithms for tuberculosis, providing a comprehensive resource for tailoring TB screening strategies to specific contexts.
